months_used: all year, with many winter evening meetings
identity: A flat, fair oval of about 1m2f
5f starts in a chute, so the minimum trip does not start on a bend
layout: A flat, left-handed Polytrack oval of about a mile and a quarter with a run-in of around two and a half furlongs.
A chute means five-furlong races start on the straight rather than on a bend.
tactics: Guides report low draws having an edge at all trips and prominent racers doing well over five to seven furlongs; the ZANS figures below test both claims.
The surface often rides fast, which can be against horses that prefer slow ground on turf.
ground: Synthetic Polytrack; going reads standard or similar.
guide_note: Low draws and prominent racers are said to be favoured, especially from 5f to 7f.
sources: IrishRacing.com, Dundalk racecourse guide (course facts paraphrased in ZANS's own words)
